cues.en: This episode of Real Engineering is brought to you by Brilliant, a problem solving website that teaches you to think like an engineer. In the past few years there has been a lot of buzz around the possibility of drone delivery services. Most think companies like Amazon will be the first to deploy them in their distribution centers, but few realize the technology is already in use for a far greater purpose in the developing world.
cues.zh: 本期 Real Engineering 由 Brilliant 赞助播出，这是一个教你像工程师一样思考的解题学习网站。在过去几年里，关于无人机配送服务的讨论十分火热。大多数人认为 Amazon 这类公司会率先在配送中心部署无人机，但鲜有人意识到，这项技术早已在发展中国家发挥着更重大的作用。

cues.en: More than 2 billion people across the world lack access to essential medical products like blood and vaccines due to poor quality or even non-existent infrastructure. Last month I visited Rwanda with Sam from Wendover Productions and Joseph from Real Life Lore. We were all struck by how modern and clean Kigali, the nation's capital was, but just a short drive outside the city, the quality of roads deteriorated quickly. The country has been working hard to improve their transportation links over the past two decades.
cues.zh: 全球有超过 20 亿人由于基础设施落后甚至匮乏，无法获得血液和疫苗等基本医疗物资。上个月，我和 Wendover Productions 的 Sam 以及 Real Life Lore 的 Joseph 一起走访了卢旺达。首都 Kigali 的现代化和整洁让我们十分惊叹，但只要开车稍微出城一段距离，路况就会急剧恶化。在过去的二十年里，该国一直在努力改善其交通网络。

cues.en: But of the 14,000 kilometres of roads in Rwanda, only 2,600 kilometres are paved. The rest consist of uneven dirt roads that become incredibly difficult, if not impossible to navigate during the country's raining season. We got a taste of this while on safari when our 4x4 got stuck in the mud, forcing us to get out and push. Keep in mind we were looking for lines on this trip. Medical supplies by nature need to be on hand quickly. If a mother is bleeding out during childbirth,
cues.zh: 但在卢旺达总长 14,000 公里的道路中，只有 2,600 公里是铺装路面。其余都是坑洼不平的泥土路，在雨季即便没有彻底瘫痪，也寸步难行。我们在一次野外考察时就深有体会，当时越野车陷进了泥潭，不得不下车去推。别忘了，我们那趟旅程原本只是去看狮子的。医疗物资天生就要求快速送达，如果一位产妇在分娩时大出血，

cues.en: she cannot afford to wait 3 hours for blood to arrive, leaving people living in remote rural villages in danger. Zipline, the real reason we visited Rwanda, is working to solve this problem with their fleet of autonomous drones, each capable of carrying 1.6 kilograms of medical supplies about the weight of 3 500 milliliter blood bags. These amazing little drones have a ton of geeky engineering design that was influenced by Zipline's design philosophies. Several unique factors influenced their designs.
cues.zh: 她根本等不起 3 个小时让血液送达，这也让偏远村庄的居民随时处于险境之中。Zipline——我们造访卢旺达的真正原因——正致力于通过他们的自主无人机机队来解决这一难题，每架无人机可运载 1.6 公斤医疗物资，大约相当于 3 袋 500 毫升的血袋。这些精巧的小型无人机融入了大量硬核工程设计，处处体现着 Zipline 的设计哲学。有几个独特的因素直接决定了它们的设计方案。

cues.en: The first is the speed the plane needs to get into the air. The moment an order comes in, the clock has started and Zipline aims to have their drone in the air in as short a time as possible. This is after all an emergency and seconds count. Currently they are averaging just 5 minutes from order to launch. That's the time it takes for an order to arrive in their onsite pharmacy to launch. But for now let's focus on some of the engineering challenges. Getting a plane into the air that quickly is pretty astounding.
cues.zh: 首当其冲的就是飞机起飞升空的速度。从接到订单的那一刻起，倒计时就已经开始，Zipline 的目标是用尽可能短的时间将无人机送上天。这毕竟是紧急救援，分秒必争。目前，他们从接单到发射起飞平均仅需 5 分钟。也就是订单送达现场药房直至起飞发射的全部耗时。不过现在，我们先来看看其中的一些工程挑战。能让一架飞机如此迅速地升空，确实令人惊叹。

cues.en: Some would struggle just to get a drone out of its case and flying in that time, and Zipline have come up with some amazing solutions to reduce those seconds. Just like a DJI drone, Zipline's plane needs a GPS connection in order to fly, as they are not piloted, they're autonomous. If you have ever flown a drone, you know it can sometimes take a little while for the drone to boot up and make a connection with a GPS satellite. So to remove that delay, Zipline moved the GPS circuitry from the plane to the battery. This means it's always on and always connected.
cues.zh: 换作一般人，在这么短的时间里光是把无人机从箱子里拿出来起飞都很吃力，而 Zipline 想出了不少绝妙的方案来争取这些宝贵的时间。就像 DJI 无人机一样，Zipline 的飞机也需要建立 GPS 连接才能飞行，因为它们并非人工遥控，而是自主飞行。如果你飞过无人机就会知道，无人机开机并连接 GPS 卫星有时需要等上一会儿。为了消除这段延迟，Zipline 直接把 GPS 电路从机身移到了电池上。这意味着它始终处于开机且保持连接的状态。

cues.en: This innovation alone removed an average of 10 to 15 minutes off the launch time. The battery is one of four pieces of the plane that need to be assembled prior to flight. First the order is placed inside the drop hatch of the fuselage, which is then placed on the launcher. The wings are then attached followed by the battery. This modular design makes the plane much easier to handle, allowing staff to easily lift it into place.
cues.zh: 单是这项创新，就让发射时间平均缩短了 10 到 15 分钟。电池是无人机起飞前需要组装的四个部件之一。首先，货物会被放入机身的投放舱门内，接着机身被放置在发射架上。随后安装机翼，最后装上电池。这种模块化设计让飞机更容易操作，工作人员可以轻松将其搬运到位。

cues.en: More importantly, it separates components so if there is a problem found with the wings during the preflight check, they are simply swapped out without having to start the entire assembly process over again. Preflight checks are often a lengthy process and Zipline have come up with some cool solutions to hasten this step too. Checking the flight surfaces is done with a mobile app that connects to the launcher system. The launch technicians simply point the phone's camera at QR codes on each control surface.
cues.zh: 更重要的是，它拆分了各个组件，所以在飞行前检查时如果发现机翼有问题，只需直接换掉，而不用把整个组装流程重来一遍。飞行前检查通常耗时很长，Zipline 也想出了一些很酷的方案来加速这一步。检查控制翼面是通过一款连接到发射架系统的手机 App 完成的。发射技术人员只需用手机摄像头对准每个控制翼面上的二维码，

cues.en: sending a message to the plane to actuate the control surface. The phone then utilizes a computer vision algorithm to make a pass or fail judgement for each control surface. Once the plane is ready and assembled on the launcher, the next time saving measure kicks into gear. Rather than telling you how this works, I'm going to show you. We spent two days at Zipline and this never got old. The rail uses a pulley and an electric motor to quickly and safely get the drone up to speed.
cues.zh: 向飞机发送指令以驱动控制翼面动作。接着，手机利用计算机视觉算法来判断每个控制翼面是否合格。一旦飞机在发射架上组装就绪，下一项省时措施就派上用场了。与其光说原理，不如直接演示给你们看。我们在 Zipline 待了两天，这场景怎么看都看不够。发射轨道利用滑轮和电动机，能快速且安全地让无人机加速，

cues.en: Accelerating the plane to its 100 km per hour cruising speed in just 0.3 seconds. It launches the same way every time and reliably clears the obstacles in front of it. Takeoff and landing are the most difficult stages of a flight. To avoid having to land at the destination, the plane simply drops the supplies in an insulated cardboard box with a simple parachute, which can then be thrown away. Meaning the clinics need no infrastructure to sign up as the client of the distribution centre.
cues.zh: 仅用 0.3 秒，就能将飞机加速到时速 100 公里的巡航速度。它每次发射的姿态都完全一致，能稳定避开前方的障碍物。起飞和降落是飞行中最困难的阶段。为了避免在目的地降落，飞机会用简易降落伞直接投放装在保温纸箱里的物资，箱子用完即可丢弃。这意味着诊所无需任何基础设施，就能成为配送中心的客户。

cues.en: When the plane does eventually need to land, the procedure to allow it to land with no pilot is even more incredible. Once again, I think it's easier to just show you how it works. It may be difficult to keep track of everything that happened there, so here it is again in slow motion. There is a small hook at the end of the tail boom, which will grab the wire strong between the two actuated arms on either side of the capture system. It's hard to see in real time, but in slow motion you can clearly see that the arms actually raise up at the last moment to catch the hook.
cues.zh: 而当飞机最终需要降落时，其无驾驶员降落的流程就更不可思议了。同样，我觉得直接演示给你们看更容易理解。刚才那一幕发生得太快可能看不清，我们放慢动作再看一次。尾梁末端有一个小钩子，会勾住捕获系统两侧机械臂之间拉紧的钢索。正常速度下很难看清，但放慢动作后就能清楚看到，机械臂实际上在最后一刻抬起去迎合尾钩。

cues.en: The plane is communicating its location in 3D space with the radio receivers next to the platform, allowing the wire to stay out of the way until the last moment, minimising any risk of collision with the wire. The capture system misses about 10% of the time, but the plane is programmed to immediately detect a miss and throttle up its engines to gain altitude and make another pass. An older design of this system had a retractable tail hook that caught an actuated wire closer to the ground, which then slowed the plane down enough
cues.zh: 飞机会与平台旁的无线电接收器通信，同步其三维空间位置，使钢索直到最后一刻才就位，将撞索风险降至最低。该捕获系统的失手率约为 10%，但飞机预设了程序，能立即检测到脱钩并推大油门爬升，进行二次复飞。该系统早期的设计采用可伸缩尾钩，用于钩住更靠近地面的活动钢索，以此让飞机充分减速，

cues.en: for it to land softly on an inflatable pad. This system was fraught with design issues. When it rained the inflatable would pool with water, which was no problem for the waterproof plane, but forced the staff to crawl through it and lift a relatively heavy plane. It was neither comfortable or ergonomic. The retractable tail boom needed a motor to control the retraction, which could fail an added weight compared to the simple metal hook attached to the carbon fiber tail boom of the current generation plane.
cues.zh: 从而平稳降落在一个充气垫上。但这套系统充斥着设计缺陷。下雨时充气垫会积水，虽然防水机身不受影响，但工作人员不得不蹚水把相对沉重的飞机抬出来。这既不舒服也不符合人体工程学。而且可伸缩尾钩需要电机来控制收放，相比现役机型直接固定在碳纤维尾梁上的简单金属钩，电机不仅容易出现故障，还增加了额外重量。

cues.en: Factoring safety into an autonomous drone network is another unique factor that has shaped Zipline's designs. Zipline works on a philosophy of redundancy of parts in order to ensure safety. It has two of everything. Two motors when it only uses one during flight, two of every actuator, and if somehow two of something breaks, the plane will automatically deploy a parachute, allowing it to softly touch down back to earth.
cues.zh: 将安全性融入自动无人机网络，是塑造 Zipline 设计的另一个独特考量。Zipline 秉承部件冗余的理念来确保安全。它几乎所有部件都是双份的：飞行中只需一个电机，却配了两个；每个执行器也配两个；即便两个都坏了，飞机也会自动弹出降落伞，平稳软着陆。

cues.en: This procedure can also be initiated by the control tower if a command from the airspace authorities is received. As a result of this focus on safety, Zipline has had zero accidents causing injury since they started service in October 2016. The next design factor, which will be common to any aeronautical design, is the weight of the aircraft and in turn its range.
cues.zh: 如果收到空域管理部门的指令，控制塔台也可以手动触发这一流程。得益于对安全的极度重视，Zipline 自 2016 年 10 月投入运营以来，从未发生过任何致人受伤的事故。下一个设计考量是所有航空设计都要面对的：机身重量以及随之受限的续航里程。

cues.en: Zipline uses planes because quadcopters use far more energy to fly, and just can't get the range necessary from batteries, and are relatively slow. These planes cruise at 100 kilometres per hour with a range of 160 kilometres, allowing the drone to serve an 80 kilometre zone around this location. The inner skeleton consists nearly entirely of lightweight carbon fibre composites, which is then covered in a lightweight foam shell which is easy and cheap to replace if it gets damaged.
cues.zh: Zipline 选用固定翼飞机，是因为四轴飞行器耗能高得多，单靠电池无法满足航程需求，而且速度相对较慢。这些飞机以每小时 100 公里的速度巡航，航程达 160 公里，能覆盖基地周围 80 公里的区域。内部骨架几乎全由轻质碳纤维复合材料构成，外层包裹着轻质泡沫外壳，一旦损坏，更换起来既方便又便宜。

cues.en: As a result, the entire fuselage weighs just 6.4 kilograms. The wings weigh 2 kilograms, with a wingspan of 3 meters. The structurally integral wingspan, that is the beam that runs along the length of the wing, is also made from high strength carbon fiber composite, with the aerodynamic surfaces being formed with high density polystyrene and 3D printed plastics. The batteries are by far the heaviest part of the vehicle, making up half of the total weight of the aircraft at 10 kilograms.
cues.zh: 因此，整个机身仅重 6.4 公斤。机翼重 2 公斤，翼展达 3 米。承载结构强度的翼梁（即贯穿机翼长度的大梁）同样由高强度碳纤维复合材料制成，气动外表面则由高密度聚苯乙烯和 3D 打印塑料构成。电池绝对是整机最重的一部分，重达 10 公斤，占了机身总重的一半。

cues.en: Zipline employed lithium-ion batteries with a total capacity of 1.25 kilowatt hours. For comparison, a Nissan Leaf has 24 kilowatt hours, and your average Tesla has about 120. As mentioned before, these removable sections aren't just batteries. They contain the GPS circuitry, but also include the data storage that hold the flight data from all the sensors on board. The moment the battery is hooked up to charge at this charging station, the data begins to pour into Zipline's servers.
cues.zh: Zipline 采用了总容量为 1.25 千瓦时的锂离子电池。作为对比，一辆 Nissan Leaf 的电池容量是 24 千瓦时，而普通 Tesla 大概有 120 千瓦时。如前所述，这些可拆卸模块不单单是电池。它们不仅集成了 GPS 电路，还包含存储机载所有传感器飞行数据的存储器。电池接入充电站开始充电的那一刻，数据便开始源源不断地涌入 Zipline 的服务器。

cues.en: For every hour of flight, these drones generate one gigabyte of data. This for me is Zipline's greatest asset. These drones don't just face engineering challenges, but regulatory challenges too. Fitting a large autonomous network of drones into an already busy and highly regulated American airspace would be incredibly difficult. Rwanda serves as not just a worthy cause, but a valuable testbed for integrating a network of autonomous drones into a country's air traffic control.
cues.zh: 每飞行一小时，这些无人机就会产生 1 GB 的数据。在我看来，这正是 Zipline 最大的资产。这些无人机不仅面临工程挑战，还要应对监管挑战。要把庞大的自动无人机网络接入原本就繁忙且管制森严的美国空域，难度极大。卢旺达不仅是一项崇高的公益事业，更是一个宝贵的试验场，用来验证如何将自动无人机网络融入国家空中交通管制体系。

cues.en: Zipline communicates directly with Rwanda's Central Air Traffic Control in Kigali Airport in the nation's capital. Having this testbed, in my mind, is more valuable than any hardware technology Zipline has developed. Ryan Oxenhorn, one of Zipline's founders, gave us a guided tour when we arrived. He's Zipline's head of software and has worked tirelessly to make Zipline's autonomous drone control system the best in existence.
cues.zh: Zipline 直接与卢旺达首都基加利机场的卢旺达中央空中交通管制部门通信。在我看来，拥有这个测试平台比 Zipline 开发的任何硬件技术都更有价值。我们到达时，Zipline 创始人之一 Ryan Oxenhorn 带我们参观。他是 Zipline 的软件负责人，一直不懈努力，让 Zipline 的自主无人机控制系统成为现有最好的系统。

cues.en: A quick look through Patons attributed to Rhine will uncover a slew of designs related to automated drone management systems, like patent 9997080, Decentralized Air Traffic Management System for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles, which describes software solutions to allow multiple UAVs which have no way of detecting other UAVs in their airspace to avoid collisions.
cues.zh: 快速翻看归于 Rhine 名下的专利，会发现大量与自动化无人机管理系统相关的设计，比如专利 9997080《无人机的去中心化空中交通管理系统》，其中描述了软件方案，使多架无法探测空域内其他无人机的无人机能够避免碰撞。

cues.en: This testbed and data is going to allow Zipline to continue to churn out designs and concepts to optimize the control of the drone delivery network, and ultimately allow them to expand into new territories with busier airspaces. This month they are expanding within Rwanda, opening a second location to serve the east of Rwanda. This could eventually grow into a supply chain, allowing drones to hop between bases, getting their batteries swapped out in a couple of minutes and beyond their way.
cues.zh: 这个测试平台和数据将让 Zipline 继续产出设计和概念，以优化无人机配送网络的控制，并最终让他们扩展到空域更繁忙的新地区。本月他们正在卢旺达扩张，开设第二个地点服务卢旺达东部。这最终可能发展成供应链，让无人机在基地间跳转，几分钟内换好电池然后继续飞行。

cues.en: This technology is useful outside of just developing countries. It could be used in disaster relief scenarios when roads become impassable due to flooding. It also allows supplies to be centralized. Hospitals often have to carry more medical supplies than they need. Keeping stocks of medical supplies with short shelf lives inevitably leads to waste. Incredibly expensive waste that costs the taxpayer money.
cues.zh: 这项技术不仅对发展中国家有用。在洪水导致道路无法通行的救灾场景中也能使用。它还让物资可以集中化。医院常常不得不储备比所需更多的医疗用品。储备保质期短的医疗用品不可避免地导致浪费。极其昂贵的浪费，花的是纳税人的钱。

cues.en: This is a problem Zipline could potentially reduce by allowing centralization of emergency supplies that can be quickly dispatched when needed. When quarantines are an issue, these drones could minimize human exposure to contagious diseases, and so help stop the spread of disease. These are both scenarios that Wendover Productions and Real Life Lore explore in their videos released today. We could not have made this trip without the help of Brilliant, so if you would like to see more videos like this, please check them out.
cues.zh: 这是 Zipline 可能缓解的问题：让应急物资集中化，需要时快速调度。当隔离成为问题时，这些无人机可以尽量减少人类接触传染病，从而帮助阻止疾病传播。这两个场景都是 Wendover Productions 和 Real Life Lore 在今天发布的视频中探讨的。没有 Brilliant 的帮助，我们无法完成这次旅行，所以如果你想看更多这样的视频，请去看看他们。

cues.en: If you have an interest in this kind of design, I would highly recommend you take this course on classical mechanics, which will form the bedrock of understanding for you to start applying physics, like figuring out how much batteries to include for a drone design. This is just one of many courses on Brilliant, with more courses due to be released soon on things like automotive engineering and python coding. If you've been inspired and want to educate yourself, then go to brilliant.org forward slash real engineering and sign up for free.
cues.zh: 如果你对这种设计感兴趣，我强烈推荐你上这门经典力学课程，它会为你打下理解基础，让你开始应用物理，比如计算无人机设计需要多少电池。这只是 Brilliant 上众多课程之一，很快还会推出更多课程，比如汽车工程和 Python 编程。如果你受到启发并想充实自己，请访问 brilliant.org/realengineering 免费注册。
